mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that lowers the risk-free rate, compressing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day period following any observation of FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp over 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive or flat returns (>=0) in more than 50% of such instances over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the most recent month, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is declining (current value below 99.0), it signals a weakening supply chain and reduced corporate output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO is below 99.0, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 5-day period following any observation of FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS declines in the most recent month, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of weak housing market activity (HOUST below 550,000 units), the S&P 500 tends to underperform, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST is below 550,000, the S&P 500 produces positive returns in more than 50% of cases over the next 20 trading days.
